design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST
The caller asks to pay for an event that is over, and nothing else. What she owes is the product of twelve declared
factors across two computations, a ledger carrying two bookings, four deposits, two guarantees, two delivered entries,
an older bill, a deposit application and a payment, a request log with an approved claim, a claim still in review and a
declined change, and a second product line's order book. The desk must also notice that the bill it is being asked to
settle has never been raised, and raise it first - a step the caller never mentions.

SCOPE CLAIMED AND WHAT REMAINS
Task 1 claims banquet_ext_delivered_event_bill (the final bill, on raise_event_final_bill_fa928380) and
banquet_ext_event_bill_settlement (what the client settles with, on settle_event_bill_79f0663f). Task 0 had already
occupied the cancellation half of the charter: banquet_ext_cancellation_notice_value and
banquet_ext_cancellation_charge_assessment with their two tools, and with them banquet_cancellation_terms as a
governing base policy. The two tasks share no extended policy, no task tool and no governing base policy: task 0's
writes are governed by banquet_cancellation_terms, task 1's by banquet_settlement_terms,
banquet_combination_venue_interaction and banquet_payment_terms. With task 1 closed, every extended policy declared in
the charter is claimed by exactly one task.

THE STEP 0 DRAW
scripts/draw_counts.py ... --tasks 2 printed {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2,
"factor_counts": [6, 6]}. The tree has exactly one prerequisite problem and both computations carry six factors.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD
Root problem: banquet_ext_event_bill_settlement - what the client settles the gala with, which is what she rang about.
Prerequisite problem: banquet_ext_delivered_event_bill - the final bill for the delivered event, which the desk raises.
Edge: kind value_input, gate bill_amount (a compute binding of the root), form state.
Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the root policy's own rule: "The amount an event bill is settled with is fixed
only after the event ledger carries the final bill for that booking, with the amount billed and the bill reference the
payment settles."
Four-point test: (1) the connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result to what it waits on; its exact
contrapositive - "the amount an event bill is settled with is not fixed until the event ledger carries the final bill
for that booking, with the amount billed and the bill reference the payment settles" - states the same dependency with
nothing added, dropped or split. The affirmative direction is how a desk states a figure that becomes fixed once the
paperwork exists, which is why it is used here while task 0's charge, which waits on the client's notice, is stated in
the negated direction. (2) The XX side is a record-visible state - an entry of a named kind standing on the event
ledger, with the two fields it must carry. (3) No tool, policy id or code token appears. (4) The strength is exact: a
hard "only after", one booking, one bill.
State form was possible and used: exactly one write in this difficulty puts a banquet_event_invoiced entry on the
ledger, the target tool of banquet_ext_delivered_event_bill. Derivation: the sentence says the amount waits on a final
bill for that booking; the ledger read shows an invoice entry only for BQ-452907; the other policy's rule says what its
result is - the final bill for an event that has been held - so the bill must be raised first, and only then is what the
client settles fixed.
Unmet at frozen_time: no banquet_event_invoiced row carries BQ-460318; the agreement's receivable balance is 0.00.
Topological order: banquet_ext_delivered_event_bill then banquet_ext_event_bill_settlement.
Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the bill moves the settlement from 68045.00 to -3475.00.
The customer never mentions it (prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint) and no tool validates it (tools_do_not_block).

BASE-INVARIANT CARD
Write 1, subject banquet_event_invoiced. Governing base policies: banquet_settlement_terms and
banquet_combination_venue_interaction. Gate settlement_state ("A final bill is only raised while the agreement stands
active or on hold...") - system_record, pre-action, correlated on banquet_agreements.banquet_agreement_id which binds
to the tool's banquet_agreement_id argument; satisfied because the agreement stands active.
banquet_combination_venue_interaction carries no structured eligibility, so it enters as policy_scope: it governs how
what the client holds elsewhere bears on the event, and imposes no state gate on raising the bill.
Write 2, subject banquet_payment_posted. Governing policy banquet_payment_terms, both gates applicable. payable_state -
satisfied on the active agreement. dispute_window is a time gate whose whole condition - "The client may dispute a
final bill no later than the dispute window for the package, counted in calendar days from the day the final bill was
raised" - this difficulty supersedes, declared in banquet_ext_event_bill_settlement.overwrite against
banquet_payment_terms: where the desk raised the bill later after the event than the days the package prints, the
window runs from the day the event was delivered instead. The gate is therefore retired rather than inherited, and the
payment write carries no base time condition; the window's own duration (30 days for this package) and its inclusive
boundary are kept, and only the day it runs from moves. On this world the window runs from 2026-08-10 and 43 days have
run against 30, so it has closed; had the desk billed inside the 14 days the package prints, the window would have run
from the bill day, 0 days would have run, and the dance floor would have been held over with the audio-visual line.
Inherited untouched: the deposit instalment rules, the guarantee deadline and overset rules, the booking rules, the
diary ceiling and the agreement state rules. Four clauses are overridden, each declared on the policy that diverges: banquet_guarantee_terms'
shortfall-billing sentence (the shortfall is dealt with at settlement instead of in the bill) and
banquet_settlement_terms' deposits-applied-before-issue sentence, both declared on banquet_ext_delivered_event_bill,
the policy that actually issues the bill, and the second of them again on banquet_ext_event_bill_settlement, the policy
that sets the money against it; banquet_payment_terms' dispute-window sentence (the day the window runs from moves when
the desk bills late); and banquet_combination_venue_interaction's same-room exclusivity (replaced by the same-day test,
on the ground the base sentence itself gives - the room is held by the booking, and it is held for the whole of the
event day - because no record on either side carries a room: the catering order carries a site code, CS-327, and the
agreement a venue code, VN-206).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
Target object: booking BQ-460318 under agreement 84a30b68-02a1-41ba-8d13-bac9539caed0 at venue VN-206 - the centenary gala of 2026-08-10. The
correlation key is booking_reference, carried by both tools; the payment additionally carries the bill reference minted
when the bill is raised. Rows belonging to it: the booking (96000.00, 400 working guests, reception), the two deposits
(33600.00 and 38400.00), the guarantee (420, 100800.00) and the delivered entry (392 served, 104000.00 consumed). Rows
of the earlier event BQ-452907 - its booking, two deposits, guarantee, delivered entry, bill INV-BQ-118204, the
13500.00 deposit application against that bill and the 21400.00 payment that settled it - are deliberately excluded
from the target object and are what the deposit pool must be read net of. On the catering account, CO-608441 is
correlated by service day (2026-08-10); CO-607920 on 2026-08-09 and CO-601238 on 2026-07-15 are the near-misses.

FACTOR CARD - banquet_ext_delivered_event_bill (6 factors, result 143520.00, whole baseline 131160.00)
1 billed_food_basis (method, multi-source). Tier: the guests served fell short of the count guaranteed (392 against
  420), so the bill is priced on the guaranteed count at the 240.00 per cover the guarantee priced to. Baseline: the
  104000.00 consumed, giving 147488.00.
2 room_rental_on_bill (parameter). Tier: the 104000.00 actually consumed reaches the 28000.00 waiver spend, so no
  rental. Baseline: the printed 2200.00, giving 145720.00.
3 production_charges (parameter). Tier: the guarantee is built to a reception, so the 2400.00 audio-visual package and
  the 1200.00 dance floor stand. Baseline: neither, giving 139920.00.
4 service_staff_on_bill (parameter, multi-source). Tier: a delivered entry stands and the served count did not pass the
  guarantee, so 35 members at 48.00 for 6.0 hours = 10080.00. Baseline: none, giving 133440.00.
5 licensed_security_on_bill (parameter, multi-source). Tier: 392 does not pass the 400 threshold but the 420 guaranteed
  does, so 58.00 for the 6.0 included hours = 348.00. Baseline: none, giving 143172.00.
6 bar_element_on_bill (parameter, multi-source). Tier: the room was taken for a reception and 392 reaches the smallest
  guest count 150, so the 4500.00 bar minimum stands in full. Baseline: none, giving 139020.00.

FACTOR CARD - banquet_ext_event_bill_settlement (6 factors, result 68045.00, whole baseline 143520.00)
1 deposit_money_set_against_the_bill (parameter, multi-source). Tier: 72000.00 stands against the booking and falls
  short of the 143520.00 billed, so all of it comes off. Baseline: nothing comes off, giving 140045.00. The 13500.00
  already applied to the February bill is the trap: counting the gross 85500.00 gives a different answer.
2 goodwill_adjustment_allowed (parameter). Tier: exactly one approved credit claim, so the single-claim percentage on
  the 100800.00 the guarantee priced to, 5040.00. Baseline: nothing, giving 73085.00. The declined guarantee change is
  the near-miss.
3 dispute_window_anchor (method, multi-source, cross-referenced by factor 4). Tier: the bill was raised 43 days after
  the event, beyond the 14 the package prints, and a delivered entry stands, so the window runs from 2026-08-10.
  Baseline: from the day the bill was raised, which leaves the window open and gives 66845.00.
4 disputed_lines_held_over (parameter, multi-source). Tier: a claim stands in review and 43 days have run against a
  30-day window, so it has closed and the audio-visual package alone is held over, 2400.00. Baseline: nothing held
  over, giving 70445.00.
5 catering_account_food_settled_here (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty: catering). Tier: the 6845.00
  hospitality suite lunch stands for 2026-08-10 and the 420 the bill was priced on passes the 250 largest guest count
  the firm's Attended Buffet Account carries, so it is settled here. Baseline: nothing, giving 61200.00.
6 attrition_covers_absorbed (method, multi-source). Tier: a shortfall of 28 beyond the 12 covers the 3 percent
  allowance absorbs, so 2880.00 comes off and the 16 covers beyond it come off at nothing, the package's shortfall
  percentage being 100. Baseline: nothing, giving 70925.00.
No stamp anywhere names these outcomes: every tier is read from ledger rows, counts, a date span, the request log and
the other account's orders and service level.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS
The guarantee and the delivered entry carry the four counts and two values the whole bill turns on; change the served
count above 420 and factors 1, 4, 5 of the bill and factor 6 of the settlement all move. The two gala deposits are the
offset; the February event's deposits and their application are what the offset must be read net of. The February bill
and its payment keep the receivable at zero and are the decoy invoice the settlement reads if the bill is never raised.
The three request-log rows are the goodwill tier, the held-over tier and a declined near-miss. The catering agreement
supplies the 250-guest ceiling and its three orders the cross-difficulty evidence with two near-misses. No cache field
exists on this holding, so no cache trap is designed; both agreement balances are exactly the sums of their account
deltas.

WHAT A CARELESS AGENT GETS WRONG
Paying against the February bill because it is the only invoice on file; billing the 104000.00 consumed instead of the
guaranteed count at the guarantee's per-cover value; charging the room rental although the waiver is met; counting
staff on the 392 served; reading security off the served count alone and charging nothing; taking the gross 85500.00 of
deposits instead of the 72000.00 standing; allowing the 35 percent ceiling for a single claim; counting the dispute
window from the day the bill was raised, which the charter supersedes for a bill raised late, and holding the dance
floor over as well; carrying the crew lunch of 2026-08-09
onto the event; and forgetting the attrition covers entirely.

STANDARD SOLUTION
Locate the firm, verify on the two details given, read the agreement, the full ledger, the request log, the catering
agreement and its orders. Work the bill: 420 x 240.00 = 100800.00 food, no rental, 3600.00 production, 10080.00 staff,
348.00 security, 4500.00 bar, 24192.00 service charge = 143520.00, and raise it. Then work the settlement: 143520.00
less 72000.00 deposit, less 5040.00 goodwill, less 2400.00 held over, plus 6845.00 same-day catering, less 2880.00
attrition = 68045.00, hand the payment to the client and let her make it by bank transfer.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN
The handling-time recomputation was executed with the gate's own evaluator over initial_state plus the replayed gold
writes. Output: banquet_ext_delivered_event_bill result = 143520.0 with factor baselines 147488.0 / 145720.0 /
139920.0 / 133440.0 / 143172.0 / 139020.0 and whole baseline 131160.0; banquet_ext_event_bill_settlement result =
68045.0 with factor baselines 140045.0 / 73085.0 / 66845.0 / 70445.0 / 61200.0 / 70925.0 and whole baseline 143520.0;
the settlement evaluated without the bill write gives -3475.0. Every figure recorded in this task is that output.

RULE / COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP
Forward: every world-reading or branching binding quotes its own rule sentence in compute_basis - the guarantee and
delivered maxima quote the pricing paragraph, the rental ladder the rental paragraph, the set-up read and the
production ladder the production paragraph, the staffing and security ladders their paragraphs, the bar ladder the bar
paragraph; on the settlement side the deposit sums and ladder, the claim counts and the goodwill ladder, the lateness
span and the anchor ladder, the dispute run and the held-over ladder, the catering sum, the account ceiling and the
food ladder, and the counts, cover value and attrition ladder each quote theirs. Backward: every load-bearing sentence
is claimed - the rounding sentences by the final RND calls, "up to the ceiling printed against the package" by the
ceiling percentage, "less anything already set against a bill or returned" by the two subtractions in the deposit pool,
"for the room on the event's own day" by the service_date filter, "before the guarantee shortfall percentage is
applied" by the attrition arithmetic. The only unclaimed sentence is the prerequisite sentence, which is the edge's
normative text.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT
With compute, expected, gold and this dossier masked, and only the published rule prose, the tool schemas, what the
finders return and the caller's lines in view: the settlement waits on a final bill for this booking; the ledger shows
none for BQ-460318; the bill policy says what the desk owes and how to price it; the bill comes to 143520.00; the
settlement then nets the deposit standing, the single-claim goodwill, the audio-visual line held over after a window
that ran from the delivery day, the same-day catering carried onto the event and the attrition covers, giving
68045.00. Same object, same order, same two numbers as gold, with no second reading available: each ladder's tiers are
disjoint as stated, and each quantity is named after the act it belongs to rather than the record it reads.

ROUND 2 - POLICY-TASK AUDIT DISPOSITIONS (revision 1 of audits/policy_task/banquet_event_desk/)
Every figure was re-derived after the change with the gate's own evaluator; nothing moved (143520.00 / 68045.00;
147488.00, 145720.00, 139920.00, 133440.00, 143172.00, 139020.00; 131160.00; 140045.00, 73085.00, 66845.00, 70445.00,
61200.00, 70925.00; 143520.00; -3475.00).

F-1 / T1-F1 (RED, closed). Symptom: base banquet_payment_terms fixes the dispute clock at the day the final bill was
raised, while the dispute_window_anchor factor moved it to the delivered day, and the base-literal reading left
66845.00 standing against gold's 68045.00. Base is frozen, so the divergence is declared: banquet_ext_event_bill_
settlement now carries an overwrite against banquet_payment_terms quoting its dispute-window sentence verbatim,
replaced by the rule's own "Where the bill was raised later after the event than the days the package prints for
raising it, and a delivered entry stands for the booking, the window runs from the day the event was delivered, the
client having had the substance of the bill at the event itself." Declaring it retires that eligibility gate, so the
payment write no longer inherits it: the dispute_window entry was removed from solvability_contract.base_preconditions
and temporal_feasibility is now empty, which check_solvability confirms (the payment's remaining gate is payable_state,
and the difficulty still exercises a base time gate in task 0's charge_posting_window). Only the day the window runs
from moves; its 30-day duration and inclusive boundary are inherited unchanged.

F-8 / T1-F2 (RED, closed). Symptom: base absorbs a catering order into an event only for the same room on the same day;
the tier tested the day alone, and no record carries a room (order CO-608441 carries site CS-327, the agreement venue
VN-206), leaving 61200.00 standing against 68045.00. Change: an overwrite against banquet_combination_venue_interaction
quoting its same-room sentence, replaced by "The room a confirmed booking holds is held for the whole of the event day,
so an order standing on that account for that day is food for that room, and the day alone settles it, whether or not
the order names the room." The persona was reworded with it: Priya now says the lunch "was for the same guests, laid
out in the same room, and that whose bill it lands on is for the desk to say and not for her" - the fact, not the
determination.

F-4 (closed). dispute_window_anchor tier 2 was unreachable: bill_lateness_days computed DAYS(delivered_day, bill_day)
before the branch, and delivered_day is empty in exactly the world that tier describes. The compute now reads
booked_event_day and delivered_entries first, takes reference_day = the delivered day where a delivered entry stands and
the booking's own event day otherwise, and measures the lateness from that; the rule states it ("The days the desk took
to raise the bill are counted from the day the event was delivered, or, where no delivered entry stands for the booking,
from the day the booking's event was to have been held") and compute_basis quotes it for both new bindings. On this
world a delivered entry stands, so reference_day is still 2026-08-10 and the lateness is still 43 days.

F-9 (closed). The override of base's "deposits applied to the final bill before it is issued" is now also declared on
banquet_ext_delivered_event_bill, the policy that actually issues the bill, replaced by "No deposit money is set against
the bill at the moment it is raised: the bill is the gross charge for the event, and deposit money standing against the
booking is set against it when it is settled." The settlement policy keeps its own declaration of the same clause for
the half it performs.

F-10 (closed). room_rental_on_bill declared the binding delivered_value and then tested billed_food_usd. The waiver is
now settled on what it declares - "Room rental is settled against the food and beverage actually consumed at the event"
- in the rule, the ladder, the compute and the basis alike. On this world the consumed value is 104000.00 and the waiver
spend 28000.00, so no rental stands, exactly as before; the factor's own baseline substitution still gives 145720.00.

F-3 (partially closed, remainder accepted). The definition sentence now says where the pool comes from: "The deposit
money the settlement draws on is what the agreement's event ledger shows taken in deposits, less anything already set
against a bill and less anything already returned." The remaining booking-scope wording is accepted: the DSL aggregates
at agreement scope by construction, and on this world the two readings coincide (the February booking's 13500.00
received and 13500.00 applied cancel, leaving the gala's own 72000.00, and all three request-log rows sit on BQ-460318).

F-5 and F-12 (closed). The docstrings of raise_event_final_bill_fa928380 and settle_event_bill_79f0663f no longer state
a later action's position, and all four money parameters now state the rounding the implementation performs.

T1-F3 (accepted). The bill is raised 43 days after the event where the package prints 14. Base carries no time
eligibility closing that window and this policy expressly contemplates a bill raised late - which is what the declared
dispute-window override now settles - so act-now remains the only defensible answer and no second value follows.

T1-F5 (noted). The audit re-derived every world assertion in this dossier and found them sound; the paragraphs it
checked are unchanged apart from the two figures the round-2 changes touched (the waiver is now stated on the 104000.00
consumed, and the dispute-window line records that the charter supersedes the base anchor for a bill raised late).
user_scenario:
Priya Lindqvist runs the managing partner's office at Kingsley Ardmore LLP, and she is the person the finance committee sends when something has to be closed out. She rings the event desk in the early afternoon with the air of someone working down a list: the firm's centenary gala was held on 10 August, the committee meets on Thursday, and she wants to settle the centenary gala today so it falls in this quarter rather than the next. She says straight out that she has the authority to pay and will put the money out this afternoon; what she needs from the desk is the figure, properly worked, and the payment on the record.

She will not read out her details unprompted. Asked who she is calling for, she gives the firm's name, Kingsley Ardmore LLP. If the agent wants more than that before discussing the account she reads her direct line, 4695117320, and then the client account code the firm bills under, CA-33182, off the header of the agreement. Asked for the billing postcode she says she is not in the office and does not have it to hand; asked when the firm's profile was opened she says it predates her and she will not guess. If the agent asks which event she means, she says the centenary gala on 10 August, the booking reference is BQ-460318, and the money should go by bank transfer from the firm's own account today.

Two things she raises only if the agent brings them up. If the agent mentions the complaint the firm put in after the gala, she says yes, the bar was shut for an hour in the middle of the reception and the desk agreed at the time that something would come off; she does not say how much and adds that she was told not to argue the point, only to get it settled. If the agent mentions a second matter the firm has raised since, she says the catering team queried the audio-visual line and she understands that is still being looked at, and she is content for whatever is still in question to sit outside what she pays now.

If the agent asks about the lunch the firm ordered for the hospitality suite on the day of the gala, she says it was for the same guests, laid out in the same room, and that whose bill it lands on is for the desk to say and not for her. If the agent asks how many people were actually there, she says the room was full but short of what they had guaranteed, and that the desk's own figures are better than hers.

When the agent tells her the amount and hands the payment across for her to make in the firm's name, she runs it while she is on the line and reads the confirmation back if asked. Once she hears the payment is recorded against the bill, she says that is one off the list and ends the call. If the agent goes quiet or quotes her nothing, she waits and asks once more where they have got to; she does not know what the figure should be and will not offer one.

seed_consistency.check: The agreement stands active on the Gala Reception Package at venue VN-206, countersigned 2025-10-01 inside the 24-month term the package prints, running to 2027-09-30; every printed figure both calculations use is read from that package column. Its deposit balance 72000.00 is exactly the deposits received (33600.00 + 38400.00 + 6300.00 + 7200.00 = 85500.00) less the 13500.00 set against the February bill, and its receivable balance 0.00 is exactly the one bill raised on it (21400.00) less the payment received against that bill (21400.00), so nothing on the agreement is past due and the 90-day credit hold threshold is not in play.

The gala booking: confirmed 2026-03-12 for 2026-08-10 at the agreement's own venue VN-206, estimated at 96000.00 with a working count of 400, which sits between the package's smallest and largest guest counts (150 and 900) and far above its 14500.00 minimum food and beverage spend. It was confirmed 151 days ahead, beyond the 60-day booking lead the package prints.

First deposit on the gala: 33600.00 received 2026-03-24, exactly 35 percent of the 96000.00 estimate as the package prints, and inside the 14 calendar days from the 2026-03-12 confirmation that the deposit due window allows.
Second deposit on the gala: 38400.00 received 2026-07-08, exactly the 40 percent second instalment the package prints, paid ahead of the 30 days before the 2026-08-10 event day by which it falls due.

The confirmed guarantee on the gala: 420 guests given on 2026-08-05, pricing to 100800.00, which is 420 covers at the 240.00 a cover the 96000.00 estimate for 400 was taken at. It was given five days ahead, exactly the 120-hour guarantee deadline the package prints, and it raises rather than lowers the working count.

The delivered entry for the gala: closed off 2026-08-11 for the event held 2026-08-10, recording 392 guests served against the 420 guaranteed and 104000.00 of food and beverage actually consumed. The shortfall of 28 covers is what the attrition allowance is read against at settlement, and the 392 served sits below the package's 400 security threshold while the 420 guaranteed sits above it.

The firm's earlier event: a theater-set reception for 150 on 2026-02-20, estimated 18000.00, confirmed 2025-12-05 at the same venue, inside the package's guest range and lead time. It is the event whose bill and payment already stand on the ledger, and it is not the booking being settled now.
First deposit on that earlier event: 6300.00 received 2025-12-16, exactly 35 percent of 18000.00 and inside the 14-day deposit due window from the 2025-12-05 confirmation.
Second deposit on that earlier event: 7200.00 received 2026-01-21, exactly the 40 percent second instalment, paid ahead of the 30 days before the 2026-02-20 event day.
The guarantee on that earlier event: 150 guests given 2026-02-15, five days ahead as the 120-hour deadline requires, pricing to 19200.00 at 128.00 a cover.

The delivered entry for that earlier event: 158 served against 150 guaranteed, 19400.00 consumed, closed off 2026-02-21. Its counts and value all sit below the gala's, which is why the gala's figures are the ones the calculations read.

The bill for that earlier event: 21400.00 raised 2026-03-05, thirteen days after the event and so inside the 14 days after the event the package prints for raising it, carrying its own bill reference and the counts it was priced on.

The deposit money set against that bill: 13500.00 applied 2026-03-05 to the same bill reference, which is the whole of the two deposits taken on that booking, leaving no deposit money standing against it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the client organisation profile from the firm's name, which is all the caller offers at first.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later lookup is keyed on the profile reference, and the caller states no internal reference.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record a passing in-session identity check on the two details the caller reads out.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing about the account may be quoted back and no money may be taken on it until this has passed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the event services agreement: its package, its state, the venue and the deposit and unsettled balances it carries.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The package fixes every printed figure both calculations use, and the agreement state decides whether a bill may be raised and a payment taken.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole event ledger: the gala's booking, its two deposits, the confirmed guarantee, the delivered entry with the guests actually served, and the earlier event that was billed, part-met from deposit and paid.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: It supplies the guaranteed count and the value the guarantee prices to, the guests served, the value consumed, the room set-up, the deposit money still standing, and the fact that no bill has yet been raised for the gala.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the event request log: which claims and changes the firm has raised on the gala and where each has got to.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: One approved credit claim sets the goodwill adjustment and one claim still in review decides which lines are held over; a third request on the log is a declined guarantee change and counts for neither.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the corporate catering agreement the firm also holds, its service level and its state.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The service level carries the largest guest count that account handles, which decides whether the same-day food is settled on the event bill or stays on the catering account.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the catering orders on that account with their service days and values.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the order served on the gala's own day is carried onto the event settlement; the crew lunch the day before and the July briefing are not.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the desk's action for raising an event's final bill.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it has no effect on the records and happens once for this action.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Raise the final bill for the delivered gala against the agreement, with its own bill reference for the client to settle.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The bill is owed on the agreement once the event has been delivered, and its amount is uniquely produced by the delivered-event bill policy.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.banquet_agreement_id: The agreement reference the agreement lookup returns for this profile: the only private event and banquet services agreement the firm holds, written against venue VN-206 and standing active. Basis: the agreement lookup returns exactly this reference; uniqueness: no second banquet agreement exists on the account.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The client organisation profile reference the profile lookup returns for 'Kingsley Ardmore LLP'. Basis: one profile matches that name; uniqueness: the agreement and the whole ledger carry that same profile reference.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.booking_reference: BQ-460318. Basis: the caller says 'the booking reference is BQ-460318', and the ledger carries a booking, two deposits, a guarantee and a delivered entry under exactly that reference for the event held on 2026-08-10. Uniqueness: the agreement carries two bookings and the other, BQ-452907, was delivered in February and has already been billed and paid.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.event_date: 2026-08-10, the day the event was held. Basis: the delivered entry for BQ-460318 carries event_date 2026-08-10 and the caller says the gala was held on 10 August. Uniqueness: the booking has one event day and the delivered entry confirms it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_amount_usd: 143520.00 — the final bill for the delivered gala. The guarantee priced 420 guests to 100800.00, which is 240.00 a guest; 392 were served, short of the guaranteed count, so the food and beverage the bill is priced on is the guaranteed count at that per-guest value, 100800.00, rather than the 104000.00 consumed. That figure is above the package's 28000.00 room rental waiver spend, so no room rental stands. The guarantee is built to a reception, so the audio-visual package 2400.00 and the dance floor 1200.00 stand, 3600.00. The guests served did not pass the guaranteed count, so service staff are counted on 420 at one per 12 guests, 35 members at 48.00 an hour for the 6.0 service hours included, 10080.00. 392 served does not pass the package's security threshold of 400 but the 420 the delivered entry was guaranteed to does, so security stands at 58.00 an hour for the 6.0 included hours, 348.00. The room the booking was taken for was set for a reception and 392 reaches the smallest guest count of 150, so the bar minimum 4500.00 stands in full. The service charge is 24 percent of 100800.00, that is 24192.00. 100800.00 + 0.00 + 3600.00 + 10080.00 + 348.00 + 4500.00 + 24192.00 = 143520.00.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the client's own settlement action so it can be handed to the caller.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it has no effect on the records and happens once for this action.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The client settles the gala bill herself in the firm's name, recording the payment against that bill on the agreement's event ledger.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Paying is the client's own act, and what she settles with is uniquely produced by the settlement policy on the ledger as it stands once the bill is raised.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.banquet_agreement_id: The same agreement reference the agreement lookup returned. Basis: the bill just raised sits under it; uniqueness: the firm holds one banquet agreement.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The client organisation profile reference the profile lookup returned. Basis: one profile matches the firm; uniqueness: the bill and the payment belong to that profile.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.booking_reference: BQ-460318. Basis: the bill raised in the preceding action names that booking, and its confirmation line states it; uniqueness: the payment is allocated to the booking the bill was raised for.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_reference: INV-BQ-963983. Basis: the confirmation line of the preceding action reads 'carried on bill INV-BQ-963983', and the invoice entry on the ledger carries that reference. Uniqueness: it is the only bill on the gala booking; the other bill on the agreement, INV-BQ-118204, belongs to the February event and was settled in March.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_amount_usd: 68045.00 — what the firm settles the gala bill with. The bill was raised for 143520.00. Deposit money standing against the booking is 33600.00 and 38400.00 taken on the gala less nothing returned; the 13500.00 already set against the February bill is out of it, so 72000.00 stands, which falls short of the amount billed and all of it comes off. One credit claim on the booking stands approved, so the goodwill adjustment is the single-claim percentage, 5 percent of the 100800.00 the guarantee priced to, 5040.00. The bill was raised 43 days after the event, beyond the 14 days the package prints, and a delivered entry stands, so the dispute window runs from 2026-08-10; 43 days have run against a 30-day window, so it has closed, and with one claim still in review the audio-visual package alone is held over, 2400.00. The hospitality suite lunch of 6845.00 was served on the gala's own day and the 420 the bill was priced on passes the 250 largest guest count the firm's Attended Buffet Account carries, so that food is settled here. 392 were served against 420, a shortfall of 28; the attrition allowance absorbs 3 percent of 420, that is 12 covers, at 240.00 a cover, 2880.00, and the 16 covers beyond the allowance come off at nothing because the package's guarantee shortfall percentage is 100. 143520.00 - 72000.00 - 5040.00 - 2400.00 + 6845.00 - 2880.00 = 68045.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_channel: ach. Basis: the caller says 'the money should go by bank transfer from the firm's own account today', and the tool's schema gives ach as the value for money sent by bank transfer from the client's own account. Uniqueness: check does not hold because no cheque is being posted, corporate_card does not hold because nothing is going on a company card, internal_transfer does not hold because the money is coming from outside rather than being moved between balances already on the firm's records, and not_applicable does not hold because money genuinely changes hands.

edges.condition: A banquet_ledger row of event family banquet_event_invoiced stands for the booking, carrying amount_usd and an invoice_reference.
edges.policy_source: The amount an event bill is settled with is fixed only after the event ledger carries the final bill for that booking, with the amount billed and the bill reference the payment settles.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-09-22 14:05:00 EDT the event ledger carries no invoice entry for booking BQ-460318. The gala was delivered on 2026-08-10 and closed off the next day, but the only bill standing on the agreement is the one raised on 2026-03-05 for the February event, which was settled in March. Read on the opening world the settlement policy takes 21400.00 as the amount billed, reads that February bill's own day as the dispute anchor and settles a figure that belongs to another event.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The desk's bill write puts a banquet_event_invoiced row on the ledger for BQ-460318 with amount_usd 143520.00, posted_date 2026-09-22 and invoice_reference INV-BQ-963983; bill_amount then reads 143520.00 and the bill reference the payment settles becomes readable from the confirmation line.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has one edge and one topological order: the desk raises the bill, then the client settles it. There are no parallel prerequisites. The order is forced rather than conventional: the settlement policy's own rule fixes its result only once an invoice entry carrying the amount billed and a bill reference stands for the booking, and the recomputation bears it out - with the bill raised first the client settles 68045.00, with it skipped the same formula yields -3475.00 off another event's bill.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the bill write and replaying everything else leaves the settlement policy reading the only invoice entry on the agreement, the February bill: bill_amount 21400.00 instead of 143520.00, the dispute anchor computed against that bill's own day, and the deposit money, goodwill, held-over line, catering food and attrition covers netted against it. payment_amount_usd moves from 68045.00 to -3475.00, and the gold payment would also quote the wrong bill reference.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions a bill, an invoice, an invoice number or the fact that none has been raised; the caller asks to settle the gala and says she will pay today. Nothing in it points at the desk's own write: she does not say 'we never got an invoice', does not ask whether anything has to be issued first, and does not prompt if the agent forgets. The only lines touching the desk's step are reactions that fire after the agent has acted: 'When the agent tells her the amount and hands the payment across for her to make in the firm's name, she runs it while she is on the line'.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: settle_event_bill_79f0663f in task_tools.py reads nothing before it writes: it computes a row id from its arguments and calls ctx.create on banquet_ledger with the payment fields. It never looks for an invoice entry, never checks that the bill reference exists, raises no error and returns the same confirmation line whatever stands on the ledger. Called on the opening world it would record a payment against a bill reference that belongs to another event, which is precisely where the failure shows up - in the terminal hash, not in a refusal.
